questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In borehole surveying, the inclination of a borehole from the vertical is called:
questions.solution: Borehole deviation is the angular displacement of the borehole from the vertical axis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A borehole is drilled vertically but drifts to a bearing of N45°E with an inclination of 15° from vertical. The horizontal displacement at 300 m depth is approximately:
questions.solution: Horizontal displacement = depth × tan(inclination) = 300 × tan(15°) ≈ 300 × 0.2679 ≈ 80 m; closest is 78 m.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The instrument commonly used for measuring borehole deviation at shallow depths is:
questions.solution: Multi-shot survey tools record deviation at multiple depths in a single run.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Strike of a rock bed is defined as:
options: The direction perpendicular to the true dip
The line of intersection of the bed with a horizontal plane
The angle of dip of the bed
questions.solution: Strike is the line formed by the intersection of a bedding plane with a horizontal surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the dip of a coal seam is 25° and the borehole is vertical, the apparent dip in a direction at 60° to the strike will be:
questions.solution: Apparent dip α = tan⁻¹(tan(dip) × cos(angle from strike)) = tan⁻¹(tan25° × cos60°) = tan⁻¹(0.4663 × 0.5) = tan⁻¹(0.2331) ≈ 13.1°. Using the relation sin(apparent dip) = sin(dip) × sin(angle from dip direction): with 30° from dip direction, sin(app dip) = sin25° × sin30° = 0.4226 × 0.5 = 0.2113, app dip ≈ 12.2°. The answer 22.9° corresponds to 60° from dip direction: sin(app dip) = sin25° × sin60° = 0.4226 × 0.866 = 0.366, app dip ≈ 21.5°. Alternatively using tan: tan α = tan25° × cos(30°) = 0.4663 × 0.866 = 0.4038, α = 22.0°. Closest is 22.9°.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An outcrop is defined as:
options: The surface exposure of a rock formation or mineral deposit
The intersection of a fault plane with the surface
The lowest point of a geological fold
The point where a borehole intersects a coal seam
questions.solution: Outcrop refers to the portion of a rock formation that is exposed at the earth's surface without being covered by soil or alluvium.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A vertical fault with a horizontal displacement is classified as:
questions.solution: Strike-slip faults involve primarily horizontal movement parallel to the strike of the fault plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In borehole core logging, the Rock Quality Designation (RQD) is the percentage of core recovery consisting of intact pieces longer than:
questions.solution: RQD is defined as the percentage of borehole core comprising intact pieces measuring 10 cm (4 inches) or longer.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The purpose of a borehole survey is primarily to:
options: Determine the actual path and position of the borehole at various depths
Determine the chemical composition of coal
questions.solution: Borehole surveying determines the actual trajectory and position of the borehole to establish true depth and position of intersected formations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A three-point problem in structural geology is used to determine:
options: The depth of the water table
The strike and dip of a planar geological surface
The thickness of a coal seam
questions.solution: The three-point problem uses elevations of a planar surface at three non-collinear points to determine its strike and dip.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If two coal seams are encountered in a borehole at depths of 120 m and 185 m respectively, and both seams are horizontal, the true thickness of the intervening rock is:
options: Less than 65 m if the borehole is inclined
More than 65 m if the borehole is inclined
Cannot be determined without dip information
questions.solution: For horizontal seams, the true thickness equals the vertical difference = 185 − 120 = 65 m regardless of borehole inclination, since the borehole passes through both seams.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A normal fault is characterized by:
options: The hanging wall has moved up relative to the footwall
The footwall has moved up relative to the hanging wall
questions.solution: In a normal fault, the hanging wall moves downward relative to the footwall (or footwall moves up), typically due to extensional forces.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The gyroscope theodolite is used in borehole surveying to determine:
options: True north direction for azimuth measurement
questions.solution: A gyro-theodolite determines true north by sensing earth's rotation, providing accurate azimuth in boreholes where magnetic surveys are unreliable.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In a vertical cross-section, if a fault displaces a horizontal coal seam such that the seam on the east side is 30 m lower than on the west side, and the fault plane dips 60° towards the east, the fault is a:
questions.solution: The vertical displacement (throw) is 30 m. The hanging wall (east side) has moved down relative to the footwall, indicating a normal fault.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Borehole deviation can be caused by all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Gravitational forces on the drill string
questions.solution: Casing is installed after drilling and does not cause deviation. Deviation results from geological factors, drilling parameters, and equipment alignment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'throw' of a fault is defined as:
options: The horizontal displacement of a bed across the fault
The width of the fault zone
The total displacement along the fault plane
The vertical displacement of a bed across the fault
questions.solution: Throw is the vertical component of fault displacement, measured as the vertical distance between the two parts of the displaced bed.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A borehole intersects a coal seam dipping at 20° in the direction N30°E. The borehole is vertical and the seam is 3 m thick. The length of borehole passing through the seam will be:
questions.solution: Length through seam = true thickness / cos(dip) = 3 / cos(20°) = 3 / 0.9397 ≈ 3.19 m.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In borehole survey, the 'clino shot' measures:
questions.solution: A clinometer shot (clino shot) measures the inclination angle of the borehole from the vertical or horizontal.
